paragraphs: 120Water sells compliance software to public water utilities and to the state agencies that oversee them. The company describes one shared system that standardizes water data and requirements into reporting and community communications. The argument for it is that utilities and agencies otherwise track assets and water quality across disconnected tools, which hurts data integrity.

The platform gathers the programs and data a team needs to manage compliance from start to finish. That includes asset records and service line inventories, sampling schedules, lab results, resident communications, and program reporting. Programs run on it include service line inventories, monitoring, school and childcare sampling, backflow, consumer request sampling, and statewide 3Ts programs. It is built to fit an existing data ecosystem, with lab integrations and APIs for syncing locations, assets, and records. Most utility and state clients onboard in weeks, with the company handling data migration, configuration, and training.

Public water systems, state drinking water programs, schools, childcare facilities, and local governments are named as the customers. The company states that every module is built with current security standards and role-based permissions meant to meet or exceed state and federal program requirements. Its stated mission is to protect public health by giving communities confidence in their water. The chief executive came from the growth equity firm Edison Partners, which the about page names as the lead investor.

quote.text: 120Water is the data management platform that brings state agencies and utilities together for water quality and asset compliance.
